components.name: Short Version
components.description: Three items under a 12rem label column, each led by a cobalt sentence-case label; the first depth of every work page.
components.html:
The short versionThree sentences, no background needed.

  1. The problem

    Community air-quality sensors have no GPS, so their location is whatever the owner typed in.

  2. The idea

    Borrow the owner's phone as a stand-in GPS and prove both share a network by timing them to a server.

  3. The result

    Registration succeeded in 4,235 of 4,238 trials with no new hardware.

narrative.overview:
This is the academic personal site done the way the best of the category does it, without a gimmick. Distill supplies the reading discipline: a serif reading column, margin notes, live figures that carry the argument. Josh Montierth's site supplies the finish: tight sans headings, hairline structure, nothing ornamental. The work is the interest. No theme ties unrelated papers together; a radon study and a stadium Wi-Fi paper share a frame, a type system and a figure runtime, and nothing else.

The surface is quiet so the figures can be loud. Tinted cool neutrals carry everything, one cobalt accent marks what you can act on, and one warm orange appears only inside figures as the second actor in an explanation. Density is moderate: generous vertical rhythm between sections (4.5rem), tight horizontal rows inside them, every list a stack of hairline-divided rows. The site is flat. There are no shadows and no cards; depth comes from a sunk fill and 1px lines.

Every work page reads at two depths: a three-item short version anyone can follow, then the full mechanism in serif prose with live canvas figures. The visual system serves that structure, and it is identical for every paper, poster and project.
keyCharacteristics: Cool tinted neutrals (hue 250 to 258) in OKLCH, with full light and dark sets on the same token names.
One cobalt accent for action and current state; one orange reserved for the second signal inside figures.
Geist for interface and headings, Source Serif 4 for explainer prose, Geist Mono for data and code only.
Hairline rows instead of cards; zero shadows.
Live canvas figures that read their colors from the CSS tokens, autoplay with pause and replay, and fall back to a still frame under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Second Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange (`signal`) lives inside figures, as the second thing being compared, and in the "Illustrative." caption marker. It never colors a button, link, heading, badge or rule on the page itself.

rules.name: The One Cobalt Rule
rules.body: Cobalt means "act here" or "you are here". If an element is neither clickable nor a current-state indicator, and it is not the first actor in a figure, it is not cobalt.

rules.name: The Shared Ink Rule
rules.body: Figures never hard-code a color. The figure kit reads `--bg` through `--bad` from the root and redraws on theme change, so a canvas always matches the page in both modes.

rules.name: The Print White Rule
rules.body: Raster figures and thumbnails were drawn for white paper; they sit on `paper` in dark mode too, framed by a hairline, rather than being inverted or filtered.

rules.name: The Three Faces Rule
rules.body: Geist for interface and headings, Source Serif 4 only for explainer prose and equations, Geist Mono only for data, code and citations. A heading inside prose is still Geist.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Years, dates, result figures and table columns use tabular numerals so they align down a column.

rules.name: The Legible Canvas Rule
rules.body: Text drawn inside a figure scales with the figure but never below 10.5px (11px in the compact home previews); on narrow screens the canvas grows taller rather than shrinking its labels.

rules.name: The Hairline Row Rule
rules.body: Lists of work, artifacts, research-area entries and CV blocks are rows separated by a 1px `line` top border, with a bottom border on the last row. The padding on these rows sits against a divider, not inside a container; a "cramped padding" flag on a hairline row is a false positive.

rules.name: The Margin Note Rule
rules.body: Asides are side comments, not callouts. They go in the right margin on wide screens and inline with a left hairline on narrow ones, in Geist at label size and `ink-3`.

rules.name: The Zero Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow. If an element needs to separate from the page, it gets a hairline or the sunk fill. The direction contract allows a shadow for menus; the build has no menus, so none is defined yet.

dos: Do take every color from the tokens on `:root` (`var(--accent)`, `f.c.signal` in figures) so light and dark both work without extra rules.
Do build lists as hairline rows: 1px `line` top border, 1.5rem block padding, bottom border on the last row.
Do set explainer prose in Source Serif 4 at the 40rem measure and keep every heading, caption and label in Geist.
Do give every new work page the same structure: header with byline and links, the three-item short version, then prose with live figures, materials and citation.
Do put a figure's tunables in its `config` block, set a meaningful `stillAt`, and mark synthetic-data figures `illustrative=true`.
Do use one primary (cobalt) button per action group and outline the rest.
Do use the house ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) at 160ms for state changes, and keep the 700ms rise-in as the site's one authored entrance.
donts: Don't use `signal` orange outside a figure, except for the "Illustrative." caption marker.
Don't add eyebrows or kickers: no small category label above a section or page heading. Breadcrumbs and the pager's Previous / Next are navigation, not kickers.
Don't use cards as structure; borders and fills frame artifacts (figures, thumbnails, citations, equations), never groups of content.
Don't add shadows of any kind.
Don't tie the work together with a themed visual concept (sensor maps, route maps, instrument dials); each piece stands on its own in the shared frame.
Don't autoplay home-page previews; they move only on hover or focus.
Don't set uppercase or letter-spaced labels; all labels are sentence case at normal tracking.
Don't hard-code colors or fonts inside a figure; use `f.c`, `f.font()` and `f.mono()`.
